style_fidelity.notes: Ref nails the painterly stipple, banded gas-giant with hand-drawn striations, and the fire/spike aura around the close-pass planet. Ours' banded planet (t02) reads as a generic red/blue gradient with no stipple; the orange sun (t14/t20/t28) is a flat radial gradient. Wobbly outlines are present but the texture is missing.

layout.notes: Ref uses one idea per card and makes the caption PART of the diagram ('SO CLOSE' overlay on planet, 'WINDS AT KM/S' on the aura). Ours t14/t20/t28 are three diagram-only beats (orbit + sun + planet) with NO caption anywhere on the card — the beat just hangs on an empty starfield. ours_t36 finally integrates caption+character+stamp, which is the closest we get to ref's discipline.

type.notes: Ours uses ALL CAPS caption typography in a single family — good match for ref. Ref's type is heavier, bolder, with thick black outline so it stays legible when overlaid on a busy diagram; ours' captions (e.g. t36 'EVERY 40 DAYS. COOKED. FROZEN. COOKED.') are smaller and feel like a separate band, not integrated into the visual.

palette.notes: Ref is disciplined: orange / yellow / black / cream. Every element in every frame pulls from that set. Ours splinters: blue orbit ellipse, red/blue banded planet, yellow sun, orange stamp, cream paper card — five different hues across six frames with no unifying logic. The HD 80606 b identity (a 'fever', a 'whiplash') should be encoded in a single hot-palette story; ours has no story.

audio_alignment.notes: ours_t14 and ours_t20 are visually identical (planet on left, sun on right, no caption) — suggests a static hold across 6 seconds of audio. ref_t113 and ref_t119 are also visually identical, so this is a wash not a regression. ours_t08 has a clean single-card character beat. ours_t36 lands the 'every 40 days' stamp card. Snap-cut discipline is okay; the issue is what each card SHOWS during its hold, not when it cuts.

biggest_gap: Caption-on-diagram integration and palette discipline. Ref overlays huge yellow ALL-CAPS text as the visual event itself ('SO CLOSE' on planet, 'WINDS AT KM/S' on planet, 'A FEVER EVERY FORTY DAYS' top-left). The caption is not a separate text band — it sits ON the diagram, and the typography is heavy enough to read against a busy background. Ours leaves multiple diagram beats (t14, t20, t28) caption-less against empty black starfields, which kills the beat rhythm. The palette compounds it: ref is disciplined orange/yellow/black/cream; ours splinters into blue ellipse + red/blue planet + yellow sun + orange stamp + cream paper with no unifying logic. The HD 80606 b identity ('fever', 'whiplash', 'close pass') should be encoded in a single hot-palette story; ours has no story. Round 3 closed stickman scale and expression variety — the remaining gap is what each card SHOWS during its hold, not when it cuts.
sub_gaps: Fire/spike aura missing: ref wraps the close-pass planet in orange flame spikes; ours' planet has no aura at all. The aura is the visual shorthand for 'this planet is being cooked'.

No stipple on planet portrait: ref's banded gas-giant has painterly stipple and hand-drawn striations; ours' planet (t02) is a smooth red/blue gradient. The stipple is half the Paint-Explainer look on planet portraits.
Header band ('HD 80606 b') missing: ref puts the planet name in a top header band on every frame; ours has no header band, so segment identity has to be re-established by the viewer each beat.
Stickman coverage: ref has the stickman in roughly half the frames; ours is in 3 of 6. The reference uses the stickman as a punctuation mark, ours uses him as a single beat.

Caption scale + weight: ref's captions are 60-80pt with thick black outline so they read against the diagram; ours' captions are smaller and live in a separate band, so they compete with the diagram instead of merging with it.
round_4_directives: INTEGRATE CAPTIONS ONTO DIAGRAMS. Stop putting the caption in a separate text band. Overlay heavy ALL-CAPS text (60-80pt, thick black outline) directly on the planet, the sun, the orbit line — wherever the visual event is. This is ref's single strongest design move and ours' single biggest miss. Target frames: t14, t20, t28 must all carry an integrated caption like 'SO CLOSE' or '4 DAYS FROM COOKED' or 'PERIHELION'.

LOCK THE PALETTE TO ORANGE / YELLOW / BLACK / CREAM. This is a 'fever' planet — the whole segment should read as heat. Remove the blue orbit ellipse, remove the red/blue planet gradient, remove the cyan anywhere. The sun is yellow/orange, the planet is orange/red, the orbit is a thin cream line, the background is black, the text is yellow or orange with black outline. Five hues max; never let blue appear in this segment.

ADD A FIRE / SPIKE AURA around the close-pass planet in t14/t20/t28 (and the t02 intro). The aura is the visual code for 'this planet is being cooked right now' — ref uses it on every close-pass frame. Ours' planet has no aura, so the viewer has to read the caption to understand it's hot. Make the heat visible.

ADD A HEADER BAND ('HD 80606 b' in 72pt wobbly hand-lettered, with the segment accent color) on every frame, not just the intro. Ref puts the planet name in a top band on every frame so segment identity is always present. Ours loses the identity between frames.

ADD PAINTERLY STIPPLE TO THE PLANET PORTRAIT. Ref's banded gas-giant has hand-drawn striations and stipple; ours' planet is a smooth red/blue gradient. Lay 1-2px black stipple dots across the banded regions before the color fill, and use 2-3 hand-jittered striation lines per band. This is the single biggest style-fidelity gap.

PUT THE STICKMAN IN MORE BEATS. Ref has him in ~half the frames; ours has him in 3 of 6. The stickman is the emotional anchor — when the narrator says 'and then it gets worse', the viewer needs to see a face react. Target: at least 4 of 6 frames should have the stickman, with the perihelion and the 'frozen again' beats both carrying character reactions.

UPGRADE TYPE WEIGHT. Ref's captions are heavy black-outlined ALL CAPS that read against any background. Ours' captions are thinner and sit in a corner band. Either: (a) overlay heavy type on the diagram like ref, or (b) if a separate band is kept, the type must be 60pt+ with a 3-4px black outline so it stays legible against the starfield.

SNAP-CUT ON THE 'EVERY 40 DAYS' BEAT. ours_t36 already gets this right with the stamp card — keep that exact pattern. The 'COOKED. FROZEN. COOKED.' rhythm needs a snap cut to a new card at each clause, not a cross-fade. ours_t36 is the round's strongest frame because it follows this rule.

DIAGRAM HOLDS MUST CARRY INFORMATION. ours_t14 and ours_t20 are visually identical — a static hold across 6 seconds of audio with no visual change. Either: (a) animate the planet along the orbit (a 6-second motion-only transition, capped at 0.2s cross-fade), or (b) snap-cut to a new diagram card at the clause break. A static 6-second hold of the same frame is a dead beat.
notes_for_orchestrator: Round 3 made real progress — stickman scale and expression variety are now in spec. The remaining gap is no longer 'character' but 'what each card shows during its hold'. ours_t36 is the proof that we CAN match ref's discipline when we try. The round_4 directives are aimed at making t14/t20/t28 look more like t36, and at locking the palette to orange/yellow/black so the segment reads as a coherent 'fever' story. If round 4 integrates captions and locks the palette, this should be a coin-flip. If round 4 does not, ref will continue to win.
